answer:
Forward records the first row-major argmax within each pooling window. Backward scatters each upstream value to that winning input coordinate. Use accumulation rather than assignment because overlapping windows can select the same input. Tied maxima use a defined deterministic convention; their mathematical subgradient is not unique. The implementation uses valid pooling without padding.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** For each pooling window $W$, $y=\max_{i\in W}x_i$ and one chosen subgradient sends upstream value $g$ to an argmax index. If overlapping windows choose the same input, its gradient is the sum of those contributions. Ties are nondifferentiable, so tests should either avoid them or enforce the implementation's documented tie rule. [3](https://d2l.ai/)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://d2l.ai/chapter_convolutional-neural-networks/pooling.html) and [2](https://cs231n.github.io/convolutional-networks/).
